chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Dawud ibn Farqad, from Yaqub ibn Shu'ayb, who said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'Should I recite in the Tashahhud: Whatever is good, so it is for Allah, and whatever is bad, so it is for others?' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'This is what Ali (peace be upon him) was saying.'
ai.seo_question: What is the recommended recitation for the Tashahhud according to Imam Ali (AS)?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi highlights the Shia practice of distinguishing between good and evil attributes during the Tashahhud, a method traced back to Imam Ali (peace be upon him). It underscores the scholarly emphasis on precise theological articulation in prayer, ensuring that praise is directed solely to Allah while acknowledging other entities appropriately. This practice reflects the broader Shia tradition of adhering to the Prophet's household's specific liturgical instructions.
